correctness.rationale: Every seed-target event on a tree has a unique directed path; chronological transmission has exact probability q^d for monotone path times. The a+b+1 distance-one and binomial-leaf distance-two paths yield invariant terms. Every left-right leaf pair contributes one directed length-three path iff its two contact marks straddle the bridge; that count is x(b-y)+(a-x)y. Algebra yields complete and strict extrema. Permutation counts yield the entire random-calendar distribution. Mark-based indicator covariance gives variance with single-pair 2/9, same-leaf covariance 1/18, distinct-leaf covariance 1/45. Replayed exact checker passed 75521 assertions for finite cases; the analytic proof covers all positive a,b and q in (0,1].

value.rationale: The full two-hub tree class gives a natural, non-arbitrary architecture for community-to-community transmission through one bridge. An all-calendar sharp scheduling rule, exact probability law and variance address real mathematical uncertainty in contact ordering beyond a toy minimum: the extreme expected-outbreak gap ab q^3/(a+b+2) grows linearly with population size for balanced hubs. The result does not imply clinical practice without empirically grounded contact and recovery mechanisms.
